why: The array index as the hash, under an O(1)-space rule: the answer lies in 1..n+1, so place each value v in 1..n at index v-1 by swapping (cyclic sort); the first index i with nums[i] != i+1 gives the answer.
hints: With a set this is easy. Which range can the answer possibly fall in, for an array of length n?
The answer is in 1..n+1, so values outside 1..n are irrelevant and each relevant value v has a home: index v-1. Can you put values home by swapping?
For each i, while 1 <= a[i] <= n and a[a[i]-1] != a[i], swap a[i] into its home. Then scan for the first i with a[i] != i+1; if none, return n+1. Each swap fixes one value, so O(n) total.
pitfalls: The swap loop condition must compare a[a[i]-1] with a[i], not a[i] with i+1, or duplicates loop forever.
Negatives, zeros and values above n are simply left where they are.
All of 1..n present: the answer is n+1.
constraints:
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
  • -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1
  • Target O(n) time and O(1) extra space (LeetCode 41 bounds; the source gives none).
